title: Model-View-Controller

validation.research: Six primary source notes: Reenskaug’s 2003 author retrospective, Krasner and Pope’s 1988 Smalltalk-80 publication, Fowler’s GUI Architectures, official Rails controller/view guides, and Python dataclass documentation. Original 1979-note URLs were unavailable, so the accessible author retrospective and historical primary publication establish the meaning without linking dead original-note URLs. The article distinguishes classic observer synchronization, explicit refresh, request/response MVC, and neighboring MVP/MVVM names. The code is original teaching material, not a Smalltalk or Rails reproduction.
validation.python_examples: Both actual article fences execute as seats.py and demo.py and produce eight stated lines exactly. Checks cover independent model validation, positive whole seat counts excluding booleans, capacity and cancellation limits, unchanged state after invalid operations, one-to-six ASCII digit parsing, malformed/oversized input and leading zeros, unknown actions, frozen/stale snapshots and their remaining-seat query, pure paired renderers, explicit refresh, headless command dispatch, independent model instances, propagated unexpected errors, and presentation failure without model rollback. Remaining-seat calculation belongs to the model snapshot; views format values only.

example_limits: Original sequential in-memory seat counter. Model methods enforce positive whole seat counts, capacity, and cancellation bounds independently of UI parsing. A controller accepts one to six ASCII digits and maps reserve/cancel actions to model operations, returning local status messages. The model snapshot supplies the remaining-seat query. Two pure text views format the same frozen model snapshot; outer composition explicitly refreshes them. Failed rules reject before mutation. No observer subscription, widget event loop, database, shared booking service, authorization, HTML output, transaction rollback, or cross-process concurrency guarantee is supplied.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, push, or pull request.
